related.name: Audio Dynamic Range & Data Rate Calculator

guidance: Geometric model only: it computes the Helmholtz tuning of a tube in a box, not the response of a loudspeaker. Use the net volume the driver sees (after the driver, port and bracing are removed), and subtract the tube's own volume, because a port that takes up air volume changes the tuning it was sized for. The 0.3 D end correction assumes both ends are free; a flared port, a slot port or a port flush with a wall tunes somewhat differently. A design that works on this page can still chuff, bottom out or sound wrong, because the driver's Thiele/Small parameters and excursion are not part of the calculation.
method: A bass reflex port is a Helmholtz resonator: the air in the tube is the moving mass and the air in the cabinet is the spring, so the port resonates at f = (c / 2 pi) x sqrt(A / (V x L_eff)), with A the total cross-sectional area of the ports, V the net internal volume of the box and L_eff the tube's effective length. Both ends of the tube open into free air, so the effective length is longer than the cut length by an end correction of 0.3 D, where D is the inside diameter; the page applies that correction itself and reports the effective length beside the cut length. The speed of sound is fixed at 343 m/s, the value in dry air at 20 C, so a colder room tunes the box slightly flat and a warmer one slightly sharp. With several identical ports the areas add and every tube keeps the same length, which is why two ports need a longer tube than one for the same tuning. The page works in both directions: given a cut length it returns the tuning, and given a target tuning it solves the same resonance condition for the effective length and subtracts the end correction to give the tube to cut. Inputs are 2 to 500 litres of net volume, a 2 to 40 cm inside diameter, 1 to 8 ports, a 2 to 120 cm port length and a 10 to 150 Hz target; decimal commas are accepted and the areas are reported per port, in total and per litre of box volume. A target that would need no real tube, because the end correction alone is already longer than the effective length, is refused rather than reported as a negative length, as is a target that needs a tube shorter than 2 cm. The page also compares the cut length with the cube root of the box volume, a rough stand-in for the internal depth, and warns when the tube will not fit straight. It models the port alone: it does not know the driver's Thiele/Small parameters, so it cannot choose the box volume, predict the -3 dB point or the excursion, or say how the port sums with the driver, and it does not model flared ends, slot ports, passive radiators, the air speed in the port or the volume the tube and driver displace. The port area per litre is shown as information, not as a pass or fail: the area a design needs depends on the driver and the playback level.

sources.title: Helmholtz resonance - the resonant frequency of a cavity with a neck is f = v/(2 pi) x sqrt(A / (V0 x Leq)) and the equivalent neck length adds an end correction of 0.3 D to the physical length

Loudspeaker enclosure - ported or bass reflex cabinets vent the rear radiation through a port tube, deliberately exploit Helmholtz resonance, and take their tuning frequency from the port's cross-sectional area and its length
